definition: A condition developing when scar tissue thickens the delicate lining around the lungs (the pleura).
general_symptoms: Difficulty or inability to take a deep breath
Shortness of breath (dyspnea), especially after or during exertion
general_causes: Empyema (buildup of pus in the pleural cavity)
Hemothorax (excess blood in the pleural cavity)
Injury to the ribs or chest
general_diagnosis_methods: Physical examination (checking for physical symptoms, such as altered breathing sounds)
Respiratory function tests (analyzing diffusing capacity and testing lung volume)
general_treatments: Many cases do not require treatment
Pleurectomy and decortication (P/D) surgical procedure (in rare, serious cases)
life_expectancy: On its own, pleural thickening usually doesn't impact life expectancy
general_outlook: Progressive disease; symptoms often become more severe over time
Long-term effects are fairly mild in most cases
Can be benign (typically will not impede normal lung functioning unless advanced)
Cannot be cured, but treatment can help manage symptoms
Not documented to be fatal on its own
Prognosis may depend on underlying condition (like lung disease or mesothelioma)

types.definition: Thickening of 50% or more of either the left or right pleura, or thickening of 25% or more of both pleurae.

specific_variant.definition: Thickening and scarring of the visceral pleura, which can lead to the collapse of the pleural space.

types.definition: Thickening confined to one or more specific areas of the pleura.

subtypes.definition: Involves the top-most portion of the pleura of one lung.
Affects the top-most portions of the pleura of both lungs.
Creates raised bump-like nodules from scar tissue.

types.definition: Affects the pleura of one lung.
Affects the pleura of both lungs.

locations.definition: The outer membrane of the lung attached to the chest wall.
The inner membrane directly covering the lung tissue.
The inner space between the visceral and parietal pleura.

related_and_underlying_conditions.relationship: Underlying condition that can cause pleural thickening as a symptom, resulting from prolonged asbestos exposure.
related_and_underlying_conditions.mechanism: Inhaled or ingested asbestos fibers get trapped in the pleura, cause chronic inflammation, severe fibrosis/scarring, and accumulating scar tissue preventing lungs from fully expanding.

related_and_underlying_conditions.relationship: Buildup of fluid between the pleurae; can cause pleural thickening or develop alongside it.
Buildup of gray/white tissue on the pleura and areas of benign thickening, most commonly in parietal pleura; distinct from pleural thickening.
Underlying condition that can cause pleural thickening.
